reasoning_content:
The problem: dockerd is running inside a cgroup that is in "threaded" mode? Root cgroup is domain threaded. Actually the container's own cgroup (/sys/fs/cgroup) is "domain threaded", which means it's a threaded subtree root. Docker creates child cgroup "docker" which inherits threaded type... Hmm, /sys/fs/cgroup/docker/cgroup.type says "threaded". Since the root here is domain threaded (meaning the parent of this container is threaded), children can only be threaded → docker cannot apply domain controllers.

This is likely because the agent container was started with cgroup namespace sharing that makes this weird. Can we fix? Options: restart dockerd with different config? The issue is the parent cgroup. We cannot modify from inside.

Wait — /sys/fs/cgroup is mounted rw. cgroup.type of root is "domain threaded"—can we write to it? Setting the root cgroup type isn't possible; the type of a cgroup is determined by its parent. Actually "domain threaded" means it's the threaded domain root — a cgroup that has both domain children and threaded children. Children with controllers enabled become domain children... Actually the rule: a threaded cgroup child of a domain threaded root can be turned into a domain if we enable controllers? No — the rule is that once a cgroup is "threaded", its descendants are threaded.

Actually the container runtime (the outer one) pretty clearly created this. Hmm but /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.type = domain threaded means this cgroup IS a threaded domain root (it's got threaded children). The docker subdir is threaded. Why was docker subdir created threaded? Docker creates /sys/fs/cgroup/docker as its own cgroup? Hmm, actually dockerd inside container often sees itself in a private cgroup namespace and mounts... Here mountinfo shows the mount at /sys/fs/cgroup is the same as the host's? It shows no cgroup namespace indication.

The typical workaround: run dockerd with `--exec-opt native.cgroupdriver=cgroupfs` — but that's the default. The error arises from systemd cgroup driver? Actually runc error "cannot enter cgroupv2 ... with domain controllers -- it is in threaded mode" happens when the target cgroup path is threaded.

Possible fix: restart dockerd with a different cgroup parent? Or move dockerd's own process into a non-threaded cgroup. Let me check: is /sys/fs/cgroup/docker threaded, but other sibling dirs? There are no other dirs. The dockerd process runs in / (cgroup.procs lists?). Let's look: cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.procs.

Actually maybe the fix is to write "+cpu +memory +pids" to /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.subtree_control — but it currently shows "cpu pids" (no memory!). Interesting: memory controller is not delegated to children. So `-m 512m` in compose requires memory controller, which isn't available in subtree_control → fail. But even without memory, docker run plain alpine also failed? Let me test: docker run --rm alpine echo ok (no limits) — with cpus. hello-world worked! So plain run works. The failure occurs when limits are requested (memory/cpus). But compose defines deploy.resources.limits.memory → docker compose translates deploy limits? With non-swarm compose, `deploy.resources.limits.memory` is applied as memory limit. Yes, docker compose applies deploy limits locally now. That requires memory controller.

Also the error message "domain controllers -- it is in threaded mode". Hmm both errors.

Wait hello-world succeeded with no limits. So containers can start. compose failed because memory limit. Can we add memory to subtree_control? cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.controllers shows "cpu io memory pids" — memory is available at this level but not delegated into subtree (subtree_control = "cpu pids"). Try echo "+memory" into subtree_control? But children of a threaded cgroup... Let's experiment.

Actually the "docker" cgroup being threaded is odd. Maybe dockerd's own cgroup is /sys/fs/cgroup/docker? No, dockerd runs in /. Hmm, but the container runtime created /docker as threaded? Let me check cgroup of dockerd pid 4: cat /proc/4/cgroup.

Alternatively, restart dockerd such that it uses a fresh cgroup? Let's investigate. Also possibility: run the stack without memory limits (remove deploy limits) — that's a modification of guide-provided compose... but acceptable troubleshooting? The task is to install & verify. We can create an override file that resets limits. But first try to make cgroups work.

Let's inspect.

action.command: cat /proc/4/cgroup; echo ---; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.procs; echo ---; cat /sys/fs/cgroup/docker/cgroup.procs 2>/dev/null; echo ---; ls /sys/fs/cgroup/docker 2>/dev/null | head; echo ---; docker info 2>&1 | grep -iE 'cgroup|runtime'
